blogs.title: How DeepSeekMath Turned Web Data Into a Math Powerhouse
blogs.description: This post would explain how the researchers built a 120B-token math dataset from Common Crawl, why data quality mattered more than just model size, and how a 7B model could rival much larger systems in math. It would focus on the paper’s data pipeline, multilingual coverage, and the surprising finding that carefully filtered web math content beat more traditional sources like arXiv.

blogs.title: Why a 7B Open Model Is Suddenly So Good at Solving Math Problems
blogs.description: This post would break down the model’s performance in plain language: what benchmarks like GSM8K and MATH actually measure, how DeepSeekMath compares with GPT-4, Gemini, and open-source competitors, and why these results are a big deal for open AI. It would help readers understand the significance of getting competition-level math performance from a relatively small, public model.

blogs.title: The Secret Sauce Behind DeepSeekMath: A New Reinforcement Learning Trick Called GRPO
blogs.description: This post would focus on the paper’s new training method, Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), and explain it without heavy math. It would compare GRPO to PPO, show how it improves reasoning while using less memory, and describe why ranking multiple answers against each other can make a model better at mathematical thinking.

blogs.title: Does Coding Make AI Better at Reasoning? DeepSeekMath Offers a Surprising Clue
blogs.description: This post would explore one of the paper’s most interesting side findings: starting from a code-trained model helped math reasoning a lot. It would explain the connection between code, structured thinking, and tool use, and discuss why training on programming data may boost a model’s step-by-step problem-solving ability beyond just writing software.

blogs.title: What DeepSeekMath Gets Right—and Where It Still Struggles
blogs.description: This post would give a balanced, accessible overview of the paper’s strengths and limitations. It would cover the model’s strong results in arithmetic and symbolic reasoning, its weaker geometry and theorem-proving performance, and what those gaps reveal about the future of AI math systems. The post would help readers see both the breakthrough and the remaining challenges.
